The company’s integrated services—from die design to final inspection—enable seamless supply chain integration, while its stringent process controls and real‑time visibility provide clients with confidence in product quality and delivery reliability. This strategic focus on quality, precision, and operational transparency secures Pentagon Forge’s reputation as a premier supplier for automotive, agricultural, and industrial markets worldwide.

products.aiLaymanSummary:
Drop Forgings are high‑strength steel parts made by a precise metal‑shaping process called closed‑die forging. Think of it as a giant, hardened “cookie‑cutter” that presses heated steel into the exact shape you need, then cools it to lock in strength. The result is a single, defect‑free component ready to drop straight into a vehicle or machine assembly—no extra machining or finishing required.

Key benefits:

- **Heavy‑Duty Strength** – Each part can carry up to 40 kg of force, making them ideal for critical structural elements in cars, trucks, tractors, and heavy equipment.
- **Versatile Materials** – Made from carbon steel, alloy steel, stainless steel, or even non‑ferrous metals, so you can choose the right balance of strength, corrosion resistance, and weight.
- **Zero‑Defect Quality** – Every batch undergoes strict in‑house testing and traceability, ensuring consistent performance and reducing the risk of costly failures.
- **Ready‑to‑Use** – Finished components arrive with standard forging tolerances, ready for OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers to assemble without further processing.

Typical use cases include automotive chassis and drivetrain parts, farm equipment components, mining and infrastructure gear, oil‑and‑gas fittings, and poleline transmission hardware. With an annual capacity of 21,600 tonnes, the factory can meet large‑scale production demands while maintaining tight quality control.

products.name: CNC Finished Forgings
products.description: Forged blanks that undergo precision CNC machining to deliver fully finished parts with dimensional accuracy up to 10 µm.
keyFeatures: Integrated heat‑treatment, shot blasting and crack detection
Turn & vertical machining centres with rotary‑tilting tables
products.aiLaymanSummary:
**What it is**  
CNC Finished Forgings are metal parts that start as solid forged blanks and then go through high‑precision computer‑controlled (CNC) machining. The process turns a rough, strong “block of metal” into a fully finished component that’s ready to be installed straight away.

**How it works**  
First, the blank is forged to give it the core strength needed for demanding applications. It then receives any required heat‑treatment (such as quench‑tempering, iso‑annealing or normalizing) to fine‑tune its hardness and durability. After that, the part moves straight into advanced CNC turn and vertical machining centres equipped with rotary‑tilting tables, where it is cut, milled and finished to within 10 µm (about the width of a human hair). Integrated shot‑blasting and crack‑detection steps ensure the surface is clean and defect‑free before the part leaves the shop.

**Key benefits**  
- **Ultra‑high dimensional accuracy** – tolerances as tight as 10 microns mean parts fit perfectly without extra adjustments.  
- **All‑in‑one processing** – heat‑treatment, surface cleaning and crack inspection are built into the workflow, reducing lead times and handling.  
- **Ready‑to‑assemble** – the finished forgings arrive at the customer’s line already machined, treated and inspected, so they can be installed immediately.  
- **Versatile for demanding industries** – ideal for high‑precision automotive components, aerospace‑grade fittings, and heavy‑duty mining or construction parts where strength and exact fit are critical.

products.name: Forgings for Tractors & Farm Equipment
products.description: High‑strength forged components used in agricultural machinery such as tractors, rotavators, harvesters and hydraulic systems.
products.aiLaymanSummary:
Forgings for Tractors & Farm Equipment are high‑strength, precision‑made metal parts that fit exactly into a wide range of agricultural machines. From steering knuckles to piston rods, these forged components are the backbone of tractors, rotavators, harvesters, and hydraulic systems, ensuring that every moving part can handle the heavy loads and harsh conditions of farm work.

The forging process shapes the metal under extreme pressure, aligning its internal grain structure to produce a component that is stronger and more reliable than cast or machined parts. Each piece is produced to OEM (original equipment manufacturer) specifications, meaning it will fit seamlessly into existing machinery without the need for custom adjustments.

Benefits for farmers and equipment manufacturers:
- **Robust construction** – withstands high stress and vibration
- **Cost‑effective** – lower production and maintenance costs compared to alternative materials
- **Precision fit** – exact OEM dimensions reduce downtime and improve performance
- **Versatile applications** – used in steering, hydraulic, and mechanical systems across many types of farm equipment

Common use cases include steering knuckles, steering arms, RD shafts, piston rods, yokes, pipe clamps, retainers, gears, gear blanks, oil seal cups, and blades. These forged parts help keep tractors and other machinery running smoothly, safely, and affordably.

products.name: Drop Forged Automotive Components
products.description: High‑strength drop forged parts for automotive OEMs and Tier1 suppliers, including steering, suspension, engine, transmission, and driveline components.
products.aiLaymanSummary:
Drop Forged Automotive Components are high‑strength, precision‑shaped metal parts produced by a drop‑forging process. In this method, a metal billet is struck by a heavy hammer or press, forcing the material into a die to create complex shapes such as steering shafts, suspension arms, engine blocks, transmission gears and driveline shafts. The result is a part that is both lightweight and exceptionally tough, meeting the demanding requirements of modern passenger cars, commercial vehicles and heavy‑duty machinery.

How it works:
- A solid metal billet is positioned in a die that defines the final shape.
- A powerful hammer or press delivers a rapid, high‑pressure impact.
- The metal flows into the die, forging the part in a single operation.
- The part is then finished to exact dimensions, ensuring tight tolerances and surface quality.

Benefits for OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers:
- **High tensile strength** – withstands heavy loads and extreme stresses.
- **Precision dimensional control** – reduces assembly time and improves fit‑and‑finish.
- **Durability and reliability** – lower failure rates and longer service life.
- **Weight savings** – lighter components improve fuel efficiency and performance.
- **Versatility** – suitable for a wide range of applications from steering and suspension to engine and transmission systems.

Use cases include passenger cars, commercial vehicles, engine assemblies and transmission systems, and these components are exported to India and markets worldwide.

products.name: CNC Finished Automotive Components
products.description: Precision CNC finished parts ready for assembly, tailored to automotive specifications.
products.aiLaymanSummary:
CNC Finished Automotive Components are high‑precision parts that are already machined, cleaned, and polished so they can be dropped straight into an assembly line. Think of them as the “ready‑to‑use” building blocks that automotive manufacturers and tier‑1 suppliers need to keep production moving smoothly. The parts are produced by computer‑numerical‑control (CNC) machines, which follow exact digital blueprints to cut and finish each piece with extreme accuracy.

**Why they matter**

- **Tight tolerances** – Every dimension is within strict limits, so the parts fit together perfectly with no extra adjustments.
- **Smooth surface finish** – The machining leaves a fine, clean surface that reduces wear and improves durability.
- **Ready‑to‑assemble** – No extra finishing or tooling required; the component can be installed immediately, cutting down lead times and labor costs.

These components are especially useful for automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and tier‑1 suppliers who need reliable, repeatable parts for cars sold in India and around the world.

products.name: Drop Forged Mining & Infrastructure Components
products.description: Field‑proven drop forged parts designed for harsh mining and infrastructure environments.
products.aiLaymanSummary:
**Layman Summary**

Drop forged mining and infrastructure components are heavy‑duty metal parts that are shaped by a high‑pressure forging process, then fine‑tuned for use in the toughest mining sites and large‑scale construction projects. The forging process squeezes molten metal into a solid shape, creating a piece that’s denser and stronger than a cast or machined part. Because the metal’s grain structure follows the shape of the part, it can handle huge forces, shocks, and wear without cracking or breaking.

**How it works and why it matters**

- **High reliability:** Each component is built to exacting standards, so it performs consistently even when equipment runs nonstop in remote, dusty, or wet environments.  
- **Durability under extreme conditions:** The forged metal resists fatigue, corrosion, and impact, meaning it can survive the heavy loads and abrasive materials typical in mines and infrastructure projects.  
- **Field proven:** These parts have been tested and used on real sites, so you know they’ve already survived the harsh conditions they’ll face in your operation.  

**Key benefits for your business**

- Fewer unexpected breakdowns and lower maintenance costs.  
- Longer service life, which reduces the need for frequent replacements.  
- Increased uptime for critical equipment, boosting overall productivity and profitability.

services.name: Custom Forging
services.description: Design and production of bespoke forged components based on customer specifications, covering material selection, die design, forging, heat‑treatment and final inspection.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Custom Forging is a specialty service that turns raw metal into precisely shaped, high‑strength parts tailored to a customer’s exact needs. From the initial design of a die (the mold that shapes the metal) to the final heat‑treatment and inspection, every step is engineered to produce components that meet the toughest performance standards.

How it works:
- **Design & die creation** – Engineers design a custom die that matches the part’s geometry and material.
- **Forging** – The die is used in closed‑die or upset forging to shape the metal under extreme pressure, creating a dense, crack‑free structure.
- **Heat treatment & finishing** – Parts are heat‑treated for strength, then shot‑blasted, fettled, and inspected for cracks and hardness.
- **Quality check** – Rigorous testing ensures each part meets or exceeds industry specifications.

Benefits for customers:
- **Unmatched strength and durability** – Forged parts are tougher and more reliable than cast or machined alternatives.
- **Custom fit** – Designed to exact specifications, eliminating the need for additional machining or assembly.
- **Material flexibility** – Works with a wide range of alloys, from high‑strength steel to specialty grades used in oil & gas or aerospace.
- **Reduced lifecycle costs** – Fewer parts, lower maintenance, and longer service life translate into savings for OEMs and equipment operators.

services.name: Engineering & Design Services
services.description: In‑house metallurgical laboratory and die‑design capability to develop engineering drawings, simulations and tooling for new forging projects.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
**What it is**  
Engineering & Design Services is a one‑stop team that combines a metallurgical lab and die‑design expertise to turn new forging ideas into real, producible parts. Think of it as a workshop where scientists test metals, engineers draw up precise blueprints, and specialists create the molds (dies) that shape the metal.

**How it works**  
- **Material testing:** Samples of the metal are examined in the in‑house lab to confirm strength, ductility and other key properties.  
- **Finite‑element analysis:** Computer simulations predict how the metal will behave under forging pressures, helping to avoid costly trial‑and‑error.  
- **Die design & prototyping:** Using the test data and simulation results, engineers design the exact tooling (dies) needed and build prototypes before full‑scale production.

**Why it matters**  
- Speeds up new product development by delivering validated designs faster.  
- Enables weight‑reduction redesigns that keep parts strong while cutting material costs.  
- Guarantees compliance with European forging standards (PED & AD2000), reducing regulatory risk and ensuring market acceptance.

services.name: Die Manufacturing & Inspection
services.description: Production of high‑precision forging dies and regular inspection using magnetic particle inspection (MPI) to ensure die integrity.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Die Manufacturing & Inspection is a service that builds and checks high‑precision metal dies used in forging. These dies shape metal parts by pressing or hammering them into the desired shape, and they must be exact and defect‑free to produce quality parts for everything from engines to structural components.

The process starts with carefully machining the die’s geometry. The surface is then hardened to make it durable. After that, a magnetic particle inspection (MPI) scan detects hidden cracks or flaws that could cause a die to fail. Finally, a dimensional check ensures every part of the die is within the strict tolerances required for high‑volume production.

**Benefits for your business**

- **Unmatched accuracy** – Guarantees that forged parts meet exact specifications.  
- **Early defect detection** – MPI catches cracks before they cause costly failures.  
- **Longer die life** – Surface hardening and precise machining reduce wear and extend service life.  
- **Higher production reliability** – Consistent, defect‑free dies lead to fewer stops and lower scrap rates.  
- **Cost savings** – Fewer defects mean less rework, less downtime, and lower overall manufacturing costs.

services.name: In‑House Raw Material Testing
services.description: Comprehensive testing of incoming steel billets and alloys to verify chemical composition, mechanical properties and compliance with international standards.
applications: Quality assurance for all forged products
services.aiLaymanSummary:
**What it is**  
In‑House Raw Material Testing is a service that checks the steel billets and alloys you receive before they go into production. By analyzing the chemical makeup and measuring how strong and tough the material is, the test confirms that everything meets the required international standards.

**How it works**  
The material is put through a series of straightforward checks:  
- **Chemical analysis** – identifies the exact elements present in the steel.  
- **Hardness testing** – measures resistance to surface indentation.  
- **Tensile & impact testing** – determines how much pulling force the material can handle and how it behaves under sudden blows.  

**Why it matters**  
- Guarantees consistent quality for all forged products.  
- Catches sub‑standard material early, preventing costly production problems.  
- Helps you meet regulatory and customer specifications without surprise.  
- Boosts confidence in your supply chain, protecting your brand’s reputation and bottom line.

services.name: Blank Cutting & Heating
services.description: Precision cutting of raw billets and controlled heating using induction billet heaters and oil‑fired furnaces prior to forging.
applications: Preparation of material for drop and closed‑die forging
services.aiLaymanSummary:
**What it is**  
Blank Cutting & Heating is a pre‑forging service that takes raw metal billets—large blocks of steel or alloy—and prepares them for the forging process. First the billets are sliced to the exact size needed, then they are warmed up to a precise temperature so they can be shaped more easily in downstream forging operations such as drop or closed‑die forging.

**How it works**  
1. **Circular‑saw cutting** – A high‑speed saw slices the billets into the exact length and shape required, eliminating excess material and ensuring a clean start.  
2. **Induction heating** – The cut blanks pass through an induction heater, which uses electromagnetic energy to raise the metal’s temperature quickly and uniformly without direct contact.  
3. **Controlled furnace heating** – For larger or more demanding parts, the blanks are moved into an oil‑fired furnace where temperature is carefully regulated to reach the ideal forging heat.

**Why it matters**  
- **Precision** – Exact cuts and uniform heating reduce material waste and prevent defects in the final forged part.  
- **Consistency** – Tight temperature control means every piece behaves the same way during forging, improving repeatability.  
- **Efficiency** – Pre‑heated, correctly sized blanks speed up the forging line, cutting cycle times and labor costs.  
- **Quality boost** – Properly prepared billets lead to stronger, more reliable forged components, enhancing overall product performance.

services.name: Heat Treatment
services.description: Full‑range heat‑treatment services including quench‑tempering, iso‑annealing and normalizing using a fully automatic continuous furnace.
applications: Strength and toughness optimisation for forged components
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Heat treatment is a set of controlled heating and cooling steps that change the internal structure of metal parts to make them stronger, tougher, or more resistant to wear. Using a fully automatic continuous furnace, the metal is heated to precise temperatures, then rapidly cooled or slowly cooled in a carefully timed sequence. This process is common for forged components that need to hold up under heavy loads or harsh environments.

Key steps in our heat‑treatment line:

- **Quench‑tempering** – Rapidly cool the metal to lock in hardness, then reheat it to relieve stresses.  
- **Iso‑annealing** – Uniformly heat and cool the part to soften it while retaining a balanced microstructure.  
- **Normalizing** – Heat the part above its critical temperature and air‑cool it to refine grain size and improve toughness.

Benefits for your products:

- **Higher strength and durability** – Parts can withstand greater forces without breaking.  
- **Improved toughness** – Less likelihood of cracking or shattering under impact.  
- **Consistent quality** – Fully automated process reduces human error and ensures repeatable results.

services.name: Shot Blasting & Fettling
services.description: Surface cleaning and finishing to remove scale, burrs and improve surface integrity before final inspection.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Shot Blasting & Fettling is a two‑step surface‑cleaning process used on forged and machined metal parts. First, the part is blasted with small steel or ceramic pellets that scrub away rust, scale, and sharp burrs. Next, a fettling step removes any remaining rough edges and leaves the surface smooth and ready for final inspection.

**How it works**
- **Shot blasting**: high‑speed pellets strike the metal, blasting away surface contaminants and smoothing the finish.  
- **Fettling**: a finer cleaning step that polishes the blasted surface and eliminates any leftover roughness.

**Benefits**
- Removes unwanted material and sharp edges, improving safety and handling.  
- Enhances the part’s surface integrity, leading to better fit, finish, and durability.  
- Prepares components for final inspection and any subsequent coating or machining steps.

services.name: Crack Detection & Hardness Inspection
services.description: Non‑destructive magnetic particle inspection (MPI) and hardness testing to detect surface/sub‑surface defects and verify material properties.
applications: Quality control for forged and machined parts
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Crack Detection & Hardness Inspection is a two‑step quality‑control service that lets manufacturers see hidden flaws in metal parts without damaging them. First, a magnetic‑particle inspection (MPI) scan is performed on forged or machined components. A magnetic field is applied to the part, and fine iron particles are sprayed or brushed onto the surface. Any crack or flaw in the metal disturbs the magnetic field, causing the particles to cluster along the defect, making it visible under a light source. Second, a hardness test is carried out on the same part to confirm that the material meets the required mechanical properties. The test measures how resistant the metal is to indentation, ensuring the part can withstand the stresses it will face in use.

Key steps of the process:
- **MPI crack detection** – magnetic field applied → iron particles reveal surface/sub‑surface cracks.
- **Hardness measurement** – calibrated indenter pressed into the metal → hardness value recorded.

Benefits for manufacturers:
- **Non‑destructive** – parts stay intact, allowing them to continue in production or be shipped.
- **Early defect detection** – cracks are caught before they grow into catastrophic failures.
- **Material assurance** – hardness data verifies that the part meets specification, reducing rework and warranty costs.
- **Improved safety** – critical components in machinery, automotive or aerospace parts are proven safe before use.

services.name: CNC Machining
services.description: Precision turning, milling and multi‑axis machining of forged blanks to deliver finished components within 10 µm tolerance.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
CNC machining is a high‑precision manufacturing method that uses computer‑controlled machines to shape metal parts. A computer program tells the machine exactly where to cut, drill or turn a piece of forged metal, so the final component matches the design down to within 10 µm (about the width of a human hair). The process works by feeding the raw blank into a machine that spins (turning), moves a cutting tool up and down (vertical milling), or tilts a rotary table to reach tricky angles, all while the computer continuously adjusts the tool’s path for perfect accuracy.

**How it works**
- **CNC turning**: the blank spins like a lathe while a cutting tool shapes its outer surface.
- **Vertical CNC milling**: a cutting head moves vertically and horizontally to carve slots, holes, or complex contours.
- **Rotary‑tilting table machining**: the workpiece is mounted on a table that can rotate and tilt, allowing the tool to reach multiple sides without re‑setting the part.

**Why it matters for businesses**
- **Ultra‑tight tolerances** (≤10 µm) ensure parts fit together flawlessly, reducing re‑work and warranty claims.  
- **Consistent repeatability** means every batch of components is identical, essential for high‑volume production in automotive, aerospace and heavy‑equipment industries.  
- **Complex geometry capability** lets you produce parts with intricate shapes that would be impossible or extremely costly with manual methods.  
- **Speed and efficiency**: once the program is set, machines run continuously with minimal human intervention, cutting lead times and labor costs.  

In short, CNC machining turns digital designs into real, high‑precision metal parts quickly, reliably, and at a scale that meets the demanding standards of today’s industrial markets.

services.name: Logistics & Export Support
services.description: End‑to‑end logistics handling, packaging and documentation to ship forged and machined components worldwide.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Logistics & Export Support is a one‑stop service that takes care of every step needed to get forged and machined parts from your factory to customers around the world. From the moment the components are ready, we handle packaging, freight forwarding, and customs clearance, so you don’t have to juggle multiple vendors or navigate complex regulations.

Key benefits include:
- **Simplicity** – One point of contact for all shipping tasks, reducing paperwork and coordination headaches.
- **Speed** – Optimized routes and customs procedures keep delivery times short and predictable.
- **Reliability** – Professional packaging and handling protect high‑precision parts, while experienced freight partners ensure on‑time arrival.

This solution is especially valuable for international OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers who need a dependable, end‑to‑end logistics partner to support their global supply chains.

services.name: Engineering & Design
services.description: In‑house R&D division provides engineering design, analysis and prototyping for complex components.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
**What it is**  
Engineering & Design is an in‑house research and development team that turns tough engineering ideas into real, working parts. Think of it as a workshop where engineers sketch, test, and fine‑tune custom components so they fit perfectly into your product.

**How it works**  
1. **CAD modelling** – Designers create a detailed 3‑D computer model of the part you need.  
2. **Finite element analysis** – The model is run through powerful simulations to see how it will hold up under stress, heat, vibration, etc., before any metal is cut.  
3. **Prototype testing** – A physical prototype is built and put through real‑world tests to confirm the simulations and spot any last‑minute tweaks.

**Why it matters for you**  
- **Tailor‑made components** – Get parts that match your exact specifications, not a one‑size‑fits‑all off‑the‑shelf solution.  
- **Better performance** – Optimized designs reduce weight, increase strength, or improve efficiency, giving your product a competitive edge.  
- **Lower risk & cost** – Early virtual testing catches problems before costly tooling or production starts, saving time and money.  
- **Faster time‑to‑market** – Rapid prototyping turns ideas into testable hardware quickly, accelerating product development cycles.

Oberlenkerhaken: Präzision für landwirtschaftliche Zugvorrichtungen

Oberlenkerhaken sind ein wichtiger Bestandteil von Zugvorrichtungen für Anhänger und landwirtschaftliche Maschinen. Sie müssen hohe Kräfte zuverlässig übertragen und gleichzeitig präzise gefertigt sein.

Wir übernehmen für diese Bauteile das Schmieden und Vergüten. Die Oberlenkerhaken werden aus Vergütungsstahl mit einem Gewicht von etwa 3 bis 5 kg präzisionsgeschmiedet. Dabei setzen wir auf teilautomatisierte Pressen und eine integrierte Inhouse-Wärmebehandlung.

Bereits in der Entwicklung unterstützen Bauteilsimulationen dabei, den Schmiedeprozess gezielt auszulegen. Durch die endkonturnahe Gestaltung lässt sich das Bauteil bereits im Schmiedeprozess möglichst nah an seine spätere Geometrie bringen. Das schafft die Grundlage für eine effiziente Fertigung und reduziert den notwendigen Materialabtrag in den nachfolgenden Bearbeitungsschritten.

So verbinden wir Prozesskompetenz, Simulation und Wärmebehandlung zu einer durchgängigen Fertigungslösung für sicherheitsrelevante Komponenten in der Landtechnik.

Was macht eigentlich ein Konstrukteur Fertigungsentwicklung bei der STP?

Für Florian Bobitka beginnt die Arbeit häufig mit einer Idee – und der Frage: Wie lässt sich daraus eine Lösung entwickeln, die am Ende auch wirklich funktioniert?

Florian kam 2021 zur STP. Zuvor war er bei Georg Fischer tätig und hatte bereits Erfahrungen im Werkzeugbau und in der Konstruktion gesammelt. Ein Tipp von einem ehemaligen Kollegen führte ihn zur STP. Nach einem Praktikum zum gegenseitigen Kennenlernen war schnell klar: Das passt auf beiden Seiten.

Heute arbeitet Florian vor allem an verschiedenen Projekten. Aktuell ist er beispielsweise an der Modernisierung von Hammer 8 beteiligt. Dabei geht es unter anderem um die Layoutplanung und die Konstruktion von Neuentwicklungen wie Robotergreifern, Artikelwagen oder Gestellen.
Ein wichtiger Teil seiner Arbeit ist außerdem die Frage, ob sich Ideen und Maßnahmen tatsächlich umsetzen lassen – und wie sich dafür eine sinnvolle Inhouse-Lösung entwickeln lässt.

Manchmal geht es dabei auch rückwärts: Beim Reverse Engineering werden alte oder defekte Bauteile, für die keine Zeichnungen mehr vorhanden sind, anhand eines 3D-Scans bzw. 3D-Drucks rekonstruiert. Anschließend wird versucht, möglichst genau nachzuvollziehen, wie das ursprüngliche Bauteil aufgebaut war und welche Materialeigenschaften oder Wärmebehandlungen erforderlich waren.

Was Florian an seiner Arbeit besonders schätzt? Kreativität. Ideen entwickeln, Lösungen ausprobieren und diese anschließend in der Projektrunde vorstellen. Dabei darf es auch einmal ein Vorschlag sein, bei dem zunächst jemand sagt: „Das haben wir noch nie so gemacht.“

Für Florian gehört aber noch etwas Entscheidendes dazu: Gute Lösungen entstehen nicht allein am CAD-Arbeitsplatz. Die Umsetzung ist Teamarbeit. Deshalb müssen auch die beteiligten Abteilungen frühzeitig eingebunden werden. Material sparen statt nur Preise senken – warum günstiger oft anders erreicht wird

Wenn es um die Wirtschaftlichkeit eines Schmiedeteils geht, liegt der erste Gedanke häufig beim Preis. In der Fertigung lohnt sich jedoch ein genauerer Blick: Wirtschaftlichkeit entsteht nicht nur dadurch, dass ein einzelner Faktor günstiger wird. Entscheidend ist das Zusammenspiel verschiedener Prozessschritte.

Auch der Materialeinsatz gehört dazu.

Ein Schmiedeteil sollte möglichst so ausgelegt und gefertigt werden, dass nur so viel Material eingesetzt wird, wie für die Herstellung des Bauteils erforderlich ist. Dabei spielen unter anderem die Geometrie, das Schmiedegewicht und die Bearbeitungszugaben eine Rolle.

Doch Materialeinsparung ist nicht der einzige Ansatz. Auch die Wahl des geeigneten Schmiedeaggregats, die Gestaltung des Fertigungsprozesses oder eine optimierte Taktzeit können dazu beitragen, einen Prozess effizienter zu gestalten.

Genau hier setzt die Arbeit des Engineerings an: Bei einer Anfrage wird nicht nur geprüft, ob ein Bauteil gefertigt werden kann, sondern auch, wie es sinnvoll in den bestehenden Fertigungsprozessen abgebildet werden kann.
Dabei geht es nicht darum, jede mögliche Veränderung umzusetzen. Die technischen Anforderungen an das Bauteil und die Prozesssicherheit bleiben die Grundlage jeder Entscheidung.

Ein gutes Beispiel dafür ist die Weiterentwicklung bestehender Bauteile: Durch Erfahrungen aus der Fertigung können sich Möglichkeiten ergeben, Geometrien oder Fertigungsabläufe innerhalb der bestehenden Anforderungen weiterzuentwickeln.

Wirtschaftlichkeit entsteht deshalb selten durch einen einzelnen großen Hebel. Häufig geht es vielmehr darum, viele einzelne Aspekte eines Fertigungsprozesses richtig aufeinander abzustimmen.

Weniger Material kann dabei ein Ergebnis guter Prozessauslegung sein – aber nicht das alleinige Ziel.

#Schmiedetechnik #Engineering #Fertigung #Produktentwicklung

India’s defence ecosystem is changing - and changing fast.

What was once largely a domain of a few large organisations is evolving into a much broader industrial ecosystem involving start-ups, MSMEs, established manufacturers, technology companies, academia, DPSUs and global partners.

Several forces are driving this transformation:

🔹 iDEX & ADITI are creating pathways for start-ups and innovators to solve real defence problems and move from prototypes towards procurement. By March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups, MSMEs and innovators, with 551 design & development contracts signed. 

🔹 Greater participation of MSMEs and private industry is changing the depth and breadth of the supply chain. Defence procurement policies are increasingly creating opportunities for Indian private industry, including MSMEs and start-ups. 

🔹 Indigenisation is moving beyond final assembly - towards components, sub-systems, materials, electronics, precision engineering, software and advanced manufacturing.

🔹 Technology is becoming central to defence manufacturing - AI, robotics, automation, additive manufacturing, drones, advanced materials and precision engineering are opening completely new opportunities. 

🔹 And perhaps most importantly, India is increasingly looking beyond “Make in India” towards “Make in India for the World.” Defence exports reached ₹38,424 crore in FY2025-26, with Indian defence products reaching 80+ markets. 

At Machine Tools India Limited, we see this transformation every day.

Our role is not simply to supply machines.

We are working closely with stakeholders across the defence and aerospace value chain - start-ups, MSMEs, established manufacturers, technology partners and global OEMs - to enable advanced manufacturing capabilities in India.

From precision machining and metal forming to complex components and quality inspection, the objective is clear:

Build the manufacturing capability in India that can compete with the best in the world.

The opportunity ahead is enormous.

The next generation of Indian defence companies are not just manufacturing for India.

They are building in India, scaling in India and exportint to the world.

And MTI is proud to be part of that journey.

CO₂-Neutralität entsteht nicht durch eine einzelne Maßnahme. Sie ist ein Weg.

Als energieintensives Industrieunternehmen wissen wir: Nachhaltigkeit bedeutet, bestehende Prozesse kritisch zu hinterfragen und gleichzeitig langfristig in neue Lösungen zu investieren.

Deshalb arbeitet die STP-Gruppe an verschiedenen Stellschrauben, um unsere CO₂-Emissionen Schritt für Schritt zu reduzieren.

Dazu gehören unter anderem:
- der Ausbau des Bezugs von Grünstrom mit dem langfristigen Ziel von 100 %
- die Installation eigener Photovoltaikanlagen
- die kontinuierliche Optimierung unserer Fertigungsverfahren
- der zunehmende Einsatz von Grünstahl
- perspektivisch der ausschließliche Bezug von Elektrostahl
- die weitere Optimierung unserer Kreislaufwirtschaft
- die Prüfung der Umstellung von Erdgas auf Wasserstoff
- die Nutzung regional verfügbarer alternativer Energien
- die Installation von Batteriespeichern

Dabei geht es nicht darum, eine einzelne „große Lösung“ zu finden. Entscheidend ist das Zusammenspiel vieler Maßnahmen – von der Energieversorgung über die eingesetzten Werkstoffe bis hin zu unseren Produktionsprozessen.

Unser Ziel: den CO₂-Fußabdruck unserer Produktion kontinuierlich zu reduzieren und die Voraussetzungen für eine klimaverträglichere Zukunft der Schmiedetechnik zu schaffen.

A proud new chapter begins for DN Solutions Global in India! 🇮🇳

Heartiest congratulations to Mr WonJong Kim, Mr. Youngsam Kim, and the entire DN Solutions team on the inauguration of their state-of-the-art 25-acre manufacturing facility in India.

This achievement also stands as a wonderful example of the Karnataka Government’s commitment to facilitating industrial growth. With the land allotted just two years ago and permissions being fast-tracked, it is remarkable to see this world-class facility up and running in such a short span of time. Kudos to Mr MB Patil, Industries Minister, Govt of Karnataka.

For Machine Tools India Limited, this is a moment of immense pride. We are privileged to be DN Solutions’ partners in India and to be witness this exciting journey with them.

We look forward to taking our valued customers to this state-of-the-art facility soon and showcasing the next chapter of DN Solutions’ manufacturing and technology journey in India.

Congratulations once again to the entire DN Solutions family!

Here’s to a stronger partnership and an even stronger future in India. 🇮🇳🤝🇰🇷

🆕 Swativo – The first pickup rake from KRONE

With the new Swativo T 1040 Pro, KRONE is now entering the world of pickup rake technology and specifically expanding its product range to include a further swathing system. While rotary rakes are particularly effective for grass and straw from stemmed crops such as cereals, pickup rakes offer clear advantages for leafy and herbaceous crops such as lucerne or clover. Thanks to the Swativo T 1040 Pro’s particularly gentle collection and conveyance of the crops, leaf loss is minimised and forage quality is further improved. This means that, in future, KRONE will offer the right swathing technology for virtually every forage plant and every application. “When developing the Swativo T 1040 Pro, the focus was not only on top-quality forage but also on consistent swath formation and intuitive ease of use – and that is exactly what we have achieved with this machine,” emphasises Tobias Reher, the product manager responsible. The pickup rake combines tried-and-tested KRONE technologies with well-thought-out design features to ensure even swathing, and, with a maximum working width of up to 10.40 m, proves to be a highly efficient link in the harvesting chain 👑
 
#KRONE #Swativo #kroneagriculture

facts.text: Official Name: Pentagon Forge & Machine Ltd.
Industry: Manufacturing
Business Model: B2B manufacturing of drop forging and CNC finished forging components for OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers

Product Name: Drop Forgings
Category: Forged Component
Description: Closed‑die/drop forged steel components manufactured in‑house and supplied ready‑to‑assemble for OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers.
Features: Weight capacity up to 40 kg per component, Manufactured from carbon steel, alloy steel, stainless steel and non‑ferrous alloys, Zero‑defect quality philosophy, Full traceability with in‑house raw‑material testing

Product Name: CNC Finished Forgings
Category: Machined Forged Component
Description: Forged blanks that undergo precision CNC machining to deliver fully finished parts with dimensional accuracy up to 10 µm.
Features: Machining accuracy up to 10 microns, Integrated heat‑treatment, shot blasting and crack detection, Turn & vertical machining centres with rotary‑tilting tables, Ready‑to‑assemble for end‑use applications

Product Name: Forgings for Tractors & Farm Equipment
Category: Forgings
Description: High‑strength forged components used in agricultural machinery such as tractors, rotavators, harvesters and hydraulic systems.
Features: Robust, Cost‑effective, Precision forged to OEM specifications

Product Name: Drop Forged Automotive Components
Category: Forgings
Description: High‑strength drop forged parts for automotive OEMs and Tier1 suppliers, including steering, suspension, engine, transmission, and driveline components.
Features: High tensile strength, Precision dimensional control, Suitable for high‑load applications

Product Name: CNC Finished Automotive Components
Category: CNC finished components
Description: Precision CNC finished parts ready for assembly, tailored to automotive specifications.
Features: Tight tolerances, Surface finish, Ready‑to‑assemble

Product Name: Drop Forged Mining & Infrastructure Components
Category: Forgings
Description: Field‑proven drop forged parts designed for harsh mining and infrastructure environments.
Features: High reliability, Durability under extreme conditions, Field proven

Service Name: Custom Forging
Description: Design and production of bespoke forged components based on customer specifications, covering material selection, die design, forging, heat‑treatment and final inspection.
Applications: Automotive OEMs, Agricultural machinery, Mining & infrastructure equipment, Oil & gas critical parts, Agricultural equipment, Heavy machinery, Industrial gearboxes

Service Name: Engineering & Design Services
Description: In‑house metallurgical laboratory and die‑design capability to develop engineering drawings, simulations and tooling for new forging projects.
Applications: New product development, Component redesign for weight reduction, Compliance with PED & AD2000 standards

Service Name: Die Manufacturing & Inspection
Description: Production of high‑precision forging dies and regular inspection using magnetic particle inspection (MPI) to ensure die integrity.
Applications: Closed‑die forging, Upset forging, Tooling for high‑volume forging

Service Name: In‑House Raw Material Testing
Description: Comprehensive testing of incoming steel billets and alloys to verify chemical composition, mechanical properties and compliance with international standards.
Applications: Quality assurance for all forged products, Quality assurance for forgings

Service Name: Blank Cutting & Heating
Description: Precision cutting of raw billets and controlled heating using induction billet heaters and oil‑fired furnaces prior to forging.
Applications: Preparation of material for drop and closed‑die forging

Service Name: Heat Treatment
Description: Full‑range heat‑treatment services including quench‑tempering, iso‑annealing and normalizing using a fully automatic continuous furnace.
Applications: Strength and toughness optimisation for forged components

Service Name: Shot Blasting & Fettling
Description: Surface cleaning and finishing to remove scale, burrs and improve surface integrity before final inspection.
Applications: All forged and machined components

Service Name: Crack Detection & Hardness Inspection
Description: Non‑destructive magnetic particle inspection (MPI) and hardness testing to detect surface/sub‑surface defects and verify material properties.
Applications: Quality control for forged and machined parts

Service Name: CNC Machining
Description: Precision turning, milling and multi‑axis machining of forged blanks to deliver finished components within 10 µm tolerance.
Applications: Automotive, aerospace, heavy‑equipment parts

Service Name: Logistics & Export Support
Description: End‑to‑end logistics handling, packaging and documentation to ship forged and machined components worldwide.
Applications: International OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers

Service Name: Engineering & Design
Description: In‑house R&D division provides engineering design, analysis and prototyping for complex components.
Applications: Custom component development, Product optimisation
